# Raffle admission and minimum buyer fee

User-approved amendment to the unfinished v3 release. Baseline for this amendment: f5f88da. No v3 deployment exists in the approved registry. Earlier fee-only evidence remains historical and must be revalidated where changed.

## Authority and acceptance

The user approved LABx approval for each raffle before sales open, covering the exact NFT and use of LABx draw funding. Sellers keep draft editing. Approval cannot change an open raffle, suppress its winner or block recovery/claims. NFT names and artwork do not prove provenance; review must identify the canonical network, collection contract, token, custody and transfer restrictions. No claim that an ERC-721 interface or code hash proves authenticity. Native non-ERC-721 assets need separately reviewed custody support and cannot be silently substituted with wrappers.

The user replaced the percentage-only buyer fee with max(2,500,000 USDC base units, floor(purchase principal * 200 / 10,000)). Principal is one purchase call's selected pack price times quantity. The minimum applies once to that call, not once per pack, and repeats for separate calls, including smart-wallet batches. Examples: 25 USDC principal costs 27.50 total; 125 costs 127.50; 200 costs 204. Seller commission remains floor(gross principal * 200 / 10,000) at settlement. User subsequently clarified that the processing fee is retained after a successful purchase. Cancellation refunds pack principal only, never the processing fee. No seller commission on cancellation. A reverted purchase keeps no fee. This supersedes all earlier full-principal-plus-fee refund requirements.

## Proposed R3 design for independent preflight

- Add immutable MIN_BUYER_FEE_USDC = 2_500_000 and append the minimum to the pinned raffle policy and opening policy hash. All quotes, approvals, ETH output amounts and actual fee counters consume the same pinned policy. Refund and treasury accounting must implement the new nonrefundable-fee policy explicitly. Require explicit minimum in the TypeScript helper, with no implicit fallback for active raffles. Existing maximum-total bound remains valid because the proportional fee exceeds the minimum there.
- Add owner-only approval of a draft after escrow. Bind approval to an expected digest covering chain, raffle contract, raffle ID, seller, NFT contract/token, NFT code hash, all editable draft fields and pack configurations, and the full current opening policy hash. Hash the bounded draft configuration directly or use a revision hash with equivalent binding. A stale review must fail, including a draft edit that is later reversed.
- Both open selectors must enforce current owner approval, unchanged reviewed draft/policy, current NFT custody and nonempty NFT code. Draft edits invalidate approval. Owner can withdraw approval only in Draft. A seller can cancel an unapproved draft and reclaim escrow. Opening consumes or freezes approval; approval revocation/changes cannot touch any later phase. Define owner-transfer invalidation before opening, so a previous owner cannot silently authorize a future owner's budget.
- Keep principal refunds separate from nonrefundable buyer fees. Define the treasury pull-claim phases, exact event semantics, cumulative fee counters, refund liabilities and seller dashboard metrics in preflight. Preserve the existing independent claims and guard against double claims, inter-raffle insolvency, fee refunds after treasury withdrawal and accidental seller commission on cancellation. Default proposal: treasury may claim collected processing fees in terminal Settled or Cancelled only. Never gate principal refunds on a treasury action. Do not silently introduce early Open-phase treasury withdrawals. Buyer review and current terms must clearly disclose that processing fees are retained even after timed cancellations.
- Approval authorizes one raffle's existing single VRF request. It does not reserve future gas prices or subscription balance. Funding review and monitoring remain operational responsibilities; approved timed refunds and permissionless finalized draw remain unchanged. No new approval check in purchase, draw, settlement or claims after opening.
- Expose exact review data and approval status through bounded pinned readers. The owner must be able to review and submit approval through the existing simulate/review/sign/revalidate transaction flow. The seller sees pending/changed/approved states and cannot publish until approved. Public details show exact collection/token and explorer links, with honest wording about LABx review rather than guaranteed authenticity.
- Preserve ABI compatibility of getRaffle's tuple, historical v2 terms and records. Since v3 is unpublished, keep version 3, update current terms content/hash and every fixture. APPROVED_DEPLOYMENTS remains empty. Do not modify archived v2 terms, deploy, fund, sign or register a live contract.
- Include the narrow Claude hardening recommendation to verify exact USDC received before crediting a USDC purchase. Preserve pull-payment isolation. Narrow overbroad mainnet copy to the guard actually implemented unless preflight recommends the existing intended Sepolia/local allowlist; do not add payee redirection, new cancellation discretion or a generic NFT support system.

## Gates

Independent Astra preflight before implementation; designated critical owner with isolated worktree; independent adversarial behavioral tests; fresh Astra final review; actual Claude review of changed contract and final website. Required regressions cover minimum crossover and rounding, quantities/split purchases, ETH parity, insolvency/under-delivery, principal-only refunds before/after treasury withdrawals, zero-principal/double refund attempts, retained processing fees after every cancellation path, seller commission only on settlement, both opening selectors, direct caller bypass, wrong owner, missing escrow, stale/reverted draft edits, policy changes, owner change, cancellation recovery and post-open noninterference. Preserve full existing regression/fuzz suites and deployment bytecode size check. Browser tests must exercise the owner-review-to-seller-open flow and mobile layouts. No main push until the complete earlier website/audit/cleanup scope also passes.

Implementation ownership and final API names will follow the preflight. Root owns integration and shared documents. No automatic on-chain actions are authorized.
